statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Nasdaq-100 conditions remain orderly and two-sided about one hour before the US August employment report at 12:30 UTC, with NQ having rejected a marginal new session high and retraced roughly 40 points inside a 0.75% overnight range.
recommendation: The assessment favours a narrow evidence-based danger window covering the payrolls release and the first hour of US cash trade rather than a session-wide restriction. Tail remains below the block threshold on currently observed evidence, and the CME weekend halt from 21:00 UTC removes live price-path exposure across the final fourteen hours of the forecast window.
headline: NQ rejects a marginal new 29,703.00 high and retraces about 40 points, with VIX at 14.16 and yields easing an hour before the August payrolls report
body: NQ futures trade at 29,662.75, about +0.47% or 138 points against a 29,524.75 prior settlement, inside an overnight range of 29,482.00 to 29,703.00 spanning roughly 0.75%. An independent quote source shows 29,658.25 with a 29,704.50 high, so the level and range agree across providers. The 29,703.00 print is a marginal new high made this hour that was not held: price has since retraced about 40 points. That is a genuine retracement rather than a shallow pullback, and overnight directional efficiency remains low, so the observed structure does not resemble the persistent no-retracement path that would threaten mean reversion. Cross-asset alignment is weak. VIX trades 14.16, down 1.12 percent, in a 14.13 to 14.25 range. The 10-year Treasury yield sits near 4.76 percent after falling from an intraday 4.818 percent on Wednesday, with the 2-year near 4.39 percent, and Treasury futures are modestly bid again this morning, so rates are easing rather than amplifying an equity move. WTI trades near 90.63 dollars, down 0.74 percent, and Brent near 95.08 dollars; both remain elevated on the persistent Middle East supply disruption but are lower on the day, and no fresh geopolitical discontinuity has been identified. Latest-session context shows the move was semiconductor-led, with the whole semiconductor group higher and technology the strongest sector, while megacap breadth was split five to three with Apple, Microsoft and Tesla lower, and application software negative. That is narrow leadership with wide dispersion rather than a broad aligned advance. The Nasdaq-100 cash index closed 3 September at 29,482.32, up 1.16 percent, after Fed Governor Waller indicated he could support holding rates steady if inflation progress continues, which reduced pricing for a September hike to roughly 50 percent from 63.2 percent. The August employment report is due at 12:30 UTC with consensus near plus 53,000 to plus 56,000 payrolls, an unemployment rate of 4.1 percent and average hourly earnings near plus 0.2 percent month on month, after July's minus 23,000. Survey estimates span minus 25,000 to plus 121,000. Because a September hike is genuinely in debate, the reaction function is inverted relative to a normal easing cycle: a strong print is the hawkish outcome. That produces a wide but genuinely two-sided distribution, which is scored as Stress and as a bounded reduction in forecast Confidence rather than as Tail, because no post-event price path has been observed. Shared cross-asset context was marginally outside its supporting freshness window at the assessment cutoff, so independent research carried the assessment; that context did not conflict with the live evidence. Tail therefore stays in the low band at 17 with the mode assessed as normal. Stress is 62 on event proximity and thinning pre-release liquidity. The danger window is kept narrow at 12:15 to 14:30 UTC, covering the release and the first hour of cash trade, and the forecast leaves the block threshold unbreached throughout because event importance and forecast dispersion are not treated as observed one-way structure.

lookbackSummary: The past 24 hours are fully covered by published Claude assessments, with no unavailable slot. The 3 September European midday was benign at Tail 13 to 15 and Stress in the mid 50s. The mode shifted to trend-up across the US cash session as the Waller-driven rally developed, with Tail peaking at 21 and Stress at 62 while the cash index closed up 1.16 percent. Overnight into 4 September the mode returned to normal and Tail compressed to a 12 to 16 band with Stress easing into the low 50s, before both climbed steadily through the European morning to Tail 17 and Stress 60 as the payrolls report drew closer. No hour in the window reached the block threshold, and the highest Tail printed was 21.
outlookSummary: The baseline holds low-amplitude two-way trade through the remainder of the European session, with Stress building mechanically into the 12:30 UTC August employment report. The release hour and the following hour, which contains the 13:30 UTC cash open, carry the widest two-sided repricing risk and are modelled at Tail 20 and 23, mapping to WATCH rather than to a block. That is consistent with treating event importance and forecast dispersion as Stress and Confidence inputs until persistent one-way structure is actually observed. From roughly 15:00 UTC the modelled path has Tail decaying as retracements reappear and volatility subsides, with a modest late-session uptick reflecting position squaring into the Labor Day long weekend. CME equity index futures halt at 21:00 UTC and do not reopen until Sunday evening, so the final fourteen slots carry no live price path; their scores describe carried weekend exposure only, and the reopen falls outside this window.
